key_insight: The paper shows that analog reliability information from inner GKP correction can decide when outer surface-code syndrome measurements can be safely skipped without harming fault tolerance.
engineering_relevance: This can lower stabilizer-measurement overhead, ancilla use, and noise injection in GKP-concatenated quantum error-correction architectures.
method: Use a surface-GKP code with adaptive syndrome skipping.
At each round, choose among four actions: measure both stabilizer types, measure only one type, or reuse prior syndromes.
Base the decision on a reliability comparison between reused syndromes and a fresh noisy extraction.
evidence_signal: Circuit-level simulations indicate the adaptive scheme reduces stabilizer measurements while keeping logical error rates comparable to or better than a full-measurement baseline, especially when gate and measurement noise exceed idle noise.
watch_item: The benefit depends on the relative noise balance and requires careful calibration of the reliability test to avoid skipping measurements when fresh extraction would be safer.
paper_title: When to Skip Syndrome Extraction in Surface-GKP Codes
